Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: The _____ was Discovery and improvement of scientific knowledge.
Basic research.fact: Basic research, also called pure research, fundamental research, basic science, or pure science, is a type of scientific research with the aim of improving scientific theories for better understanding and prediction of natural or other phenomena. Though often driven simply by curiosity, basic research often fuels the technological innovations of applied science.

Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: The National Natural Science Foundation of _____ (NSFC) serves as the principal agency funding investigator-driven fundamental research across the natural sciences and engineering
Basic research.fact: The National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC) serves as the principal agency funding investigator-driven fundamental research across the natural sciences and engineering. China’s gross domestic expenditure on research and development (R&D) has increased substantially since the early 2000s and exceeds 2% of GDP.

Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: China’s gross domestic expenditure on research and development (R&D) has increased substantially since the early 2000s and exceeds _____ of GDP
Basic research.fact: China’s gross domestic expenditure on research and development (R&D) has increased substantially since the early 2000s and exceeds 2% of GDP.

Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: The Department of Science and Technology (DST) and the Science and _____ (SERB) provide competitive grants supporting fundamental scientific research
Basic research.fact: The Department of Science and Technology (DST) and the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB) provide competitive grants supporting fundamental scientific research.

Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: Research is also conducted in national laboratories operated by the Council of Scientific and _____ (CSIR), which supports both basic and applied scientific investigation
Basic research.fact: Research is also conducted in national laboratories operated by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), which supports both basic and applied scientific investigation.

Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: The National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF), established under the _____ of Science and ICT, administers competitive grants supporting fundamental research in science and engineering
Basic research.fact: National policy coordination for science and technology is conducted by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), which supports universities and national research institutes engaged in basic research. The National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF), set up under the Ministry of Science and ICT, administers competitive grants supporting fundamental research in science and engineering.

Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: South Korea has maintained one of the highest levels of gross domestic expenditure on research and development (R&D) relative to GDP among _____ countries
Basic research.fact: South Korea has maintained one of the highest levels of gross domestic expenditure on research and development (R&D) relative to GDP among OECD countries.

Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: UK researchers participate in _____ framework programmes such as Horizon Europe, which fund collaborative and frontier research projects
Basic research.fact: UK researchers participate in European framework programmes such as Horizon Europe, which fund collaborative and frontier research projects.

Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: Roughly _____ of basic research is conducted by universities
Basic research.fact: Roughly 76% of basic research is conducted by universities.

Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: They can be grouped as STM (science, technology, and medicine; not to be confused with _____ [science, technology, engineering, and mathematics]) or STS (science, technology, and society)
Basic research.fact: They can be grouped as STM (science, technology, and medicine; not to be confused with STEM [science, technology, engineering, and mathematics]) or STS (science, technology, and society).

Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: The Nobel Prize mixes basic with applied sciences for its award in _____ or Medicine
Basic research.fact: The Nobel Prize mixes basic with applied sciences for its award in Physiology or Medicine.

Basic research.subject: Applied Sciences
Basic research.question: In contrast, the _____ of London awards distinguish natural science from applied science
Basic research.fact: In contrast, the Royal Society of London awards distinguish natural science from applied science.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: The _____ was Methods for numerical approximations.
Numerical analysis.fact: Numerical analysis is the study of algorithms for the problems of continuous mathematics. Numerical analysis finds application in all fields of engineering and the physical sciences, and in the 21st century also the life and social sciences like economics, medicine, business and even the arts.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: A tablet from the _____ (YBC 7289), gives a sexagesimal numerical approximation of the square root of 2, the length of the diagonal in a unit square
Numerical analysis.fact: A tablet from the Yale Babylonian Collection (YBC 7289), gives a sexagesimal numerical approximation of the square root of 2, the length of the diagonal in a unit square.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: Linear interpolation was already in use more than _____ years ago
Numerical analysis.fact: Linear interpolation was already in use more than 2000 years ago.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: The origins of modern numerical analysis are often linked to a _____ paper by John von Neumann and Herman Goldstine, but others consider modern numerical analysis to go back to work by E. T. Whittaker
Numerical analysis.fact: The origins of modern numerical analysis are often linked to a 1947 paper by John von Neumann and Herman Goldstine, but others consider modern numerical analysis to go back to work by E. T. Whittaker in 1912.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: The canonical work in the field is the NIST publication edited by Abramowitz and Stegun, a _____-plus page book of a very large number of commonly used formulas and functions and their values at many
Numerical analysis.fact: The canonical work in the field is the NIST publication edited by Abramowitz and Stegun, a 1000-plus page book of a very large number of commonly used formulas and functions and their values at many points.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: The Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis was initiated in _____ by the Institute of Mathematics and its Applications
Numerical analysis.fact: The Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis was initiated in 1985 by the Institute of Mathematics and its Applications.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: Examples include _____ elimination, the QR factorization method for solving systems of linear equations, and the simplex method of linear programming
Numerical analysis.fact: Examples include Gaussian elimination, the QR factorization method for solving systems of linear equations, and the simplex method of linear programming.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: Examples include _____'s method, the bisection method, and Jacobi iteration
Numerical analysis.fact: Examples include Newton's method, the bisection method, and Jacobi iteration.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: Note that f(1.1) = 10 and f(1.001) = _____: a change in x of less than 0.1 turns into a change in f(x) of nearly 1000
Numerical analysis.fact: Note that f(1.1) = 10 and f(1.001) = 1000: a change in x of less than 0.1 turns into a change in f(x) of nearly 1000.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: For polynomials, a better approach is using the _____ scheme, since it reduces the necessary number of multiplications and additions
Numerical analysis.fact: For polynomials, a better approach is using the Horner scheme, since it reduces the necessary number of multiplications and additions.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: Iterative methods such as the _____ method, Gauss–Seidel method, successive over-relaxation and conjugate gradient method are usually preferred for large systems
Numerical analysis.fact: Iterative methods such as the Jacobi method, Gauss–Seidel method, successive over-relaxation and conjugate gradient method are usually preferred for large systems.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: If the function is differentiable and the derivative is known, then _____'s method is a popular choice
Numerical analysis.fact: If the function is differentiable and the derivative is known, then Newton's method is a popular choice.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: The method of _____ multipliers can be used to reduce optimization problems with constraints to unconstrained optimization problems
Numerical analysis.fact: The method of Lagrange multipliers can be used to reduce optimization problems with constraints to unconstrained optimization problems.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: Popular methods use one of the Newton–Cotes formulas (like the midpoint rule or _____'s rule) or Gaussian quadrature
Numerical analysis.fact: Popular methods use one of the Newton–Cotes formulas (like the midpoint rule or Simpson's rule) or Gaussian quadrature.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: The Naval Surface Warfare Center several times published its Library of _____ (code here)
Numerical analysis.fact: The Naval Surface Warfare Center several times published its Library of Mathematics Subroutines (code here).

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences

Numerical analysis.fact: There are also programming languages such as R (similar to S-PLUS), Julia, and Python with libraries such as NumPy, SciPy and SymPy.

Numerical analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Numerical analysis.question: Many computer algebra systems such as _____ also benefit from the availability of arbitrary-precision arithmetic which can provide more accurate results
Numerical analysis.fact: Many computer algebra systems such as Mathematica also benefit from the availability of arbitrary-precision arithmetic which can provide more accurate results.

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences
Calculus.question: The _____ was Branch of mathematics.
Calculus.fact: Calculus is the branch of mathematics that studies continuous change, and is the principal precursor of modern mathematical analysis. Originally called infinitesimal calculus or the calculus of infinitesimals, it has two major branches, differential calculus and integral calculus.

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences
Calculus.question: The word calculate was used in English in this sense at least as early as _____, several years before the publications of Leibniz and Newton, who wrote their mathematical texts in Latin
Calculus.fact: The word calculate was used in English in this sense at least as early as 1672, several years before the publications of Leibniz and Newton, who wrote their mathematical texts in Latin.

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences
Calculus.question: {\displaystyle m={\frac {\text{rise}}{\text{run}}}={\frac {{\text{change in }}y}{{\text{change in }}x}}={\frac {\_____ y}{\Delta x}}.} This gives an exact value for the slope of a straight line
Calculus.fact: {\displaystyle m={\frac {\text{rise}}{\text{run}}}={\frac {{\text{change in }}y}{{\text{change in }}x}}={\frac {\Delta y}{\Delta x}}.} This gives an exact value for the slope of a straight line.

Calculus.fact: {\displaystyle \lim _{h\to 0}{f(a+h)-f(a) \over {h}}.} Geometrically, the derivative is the slope of the tangent line to the graph of f at a.

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences
Calculus.question: The technical definition of the definite integral involves the limit of a sum of areas of rectangles, called a _____ sum
Calculus.fact: The technical definition of the definite integral involves the limit of a sum of areas of rectangles, called a Riemann sum. Calculus.fact: For example, traveling a steady 50 mph for 3 hours results in a total distance of 150 miles.

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences
Calculus.question: Bonaventura Cavalieri, basing his work on _____'s, argued that volumes and areas should be computed as the sums of the volumes and areas of infinitesimally thin cross-sections
Calculus.fact: Kepler developed a method to calculate the area of an ellipse by adding up the lengths of many radii drawn from a focus of the ellipse. Bonaventura Cavalieri, basing his work on Kepler's, argued that volumes and areas should be computed as the sums of the volumes and areas of infinitesimally thin cross-sections.

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences

Calculus.fact: Pierre de Fermat, claiming that he borrowed from Diophantus, introduced the concept of adequality, which represented equality up to an infinitesimal error term.

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences

Calculus.fact: The combination was achieved by John Wallis, Isaac Barrow, and James Gregory, the latter two proving part of the fundamental theorem of calculus around 1670.

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences

Calculus.fact: The product rule and chain rule, the notions of higher derivatives and Taylor series, and of analytic functions were used by Isaac Newton in an idiosyncratic notation which he applied to solve problems of mathematical physics. Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences

Calculus.fact: The product rule and chain rule, the notions of higher derivatives and Taylor series, and of analytic functions were used by Isaac Newton in an idiosyncratic notation which he applied to solve problems of mathematical physics. Calculus.fact: Leibniz developed much of the notation used in calculus today. Calculus.fact: This controversy divided English-speaking mathematicians from continental European mathematicians for many years, to the detriment of English mathematics. Newton called his calculus "the science of fluxions", a term that endured in English schools into the 19th century.

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences
Calculus.question: A careful examination of the papers of _____ and Newton shows that they arrived at their results independently, with Leibniz starting first with integration and Newton with differentiation

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences
Calculus.question: It is _____, however, who gave the new discipline its name
Calculus.fact: Newton claimed Leibniz stole ideas from his unpublished notes, which Newton had shared with a few members of the Royal Society. A careful examination of the papers of Leibniz and Newton shows that they arrived at their results independently, with Leibniz starting first with integration and Newton with differentiation.

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences

Calculus.fact: The first complete treatise on calculus to be written in English and use the Leibniz notation was not published until 1815.

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences

Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences

Calculus.fact: Several mathematicians, including Maclaurin, tried to prove the soundness of using infinitesimals, but it would not be until 150 years later when, due to the work of Cauchy and Weierstrass, a way was finally found to avoid mere "notions" of infinitely small quantities. Calculus.subject: Applied Sciences

Calculus.fact: For instance, spacecraft use a variation of the Euler method to approximate curved courses within zero-gravity environments.

Differential equation.subject: Applied Sciences
Differential equation.question: The _____ was Type of functional equation (mathematics).
Differential equation.fact: In mathematics, a differential equation is an equation that relates one or more unknown functions and their derivatives. In applications, the functions generally represent physical quantities, the derivatives represent their rates of change, and the differential equation defines a relationship between the two.

Differential equation.subject: Applied Sciences

Differential equation.fact: Jacob Bernoulli proposed the Bernoulli differential equation in 1695.

Differential equation.fact: Historically, the problem of a vibrating string such as that of a musical instrument was studied by Jean le Rond d'Alembert, Leonhard Euler, Daniel Bernoulli, and Joseph-Louis Lagrange.

Differential equation.subject: Applied Sciences

Blaise Pascal.fact: Blaise Pascal (19 June 1623 – 19 August 1662) was a French mathematician, physicist, inventor, philosopher, and Catholic writer.

Blaise Pascal.subject: Applied Sciences
Blaise Pascal.question: In _____, he started some pioneering work on calculating machines (called Pascal's calculators and later Pascalines), establishing him as one of the first two inventors of the mechanical calculator
Blaise Pascal.fact: In 1642, he started some pioneering work on calculating machines (called Pascal's calculators and later Pascalines), establishing him as one of the first two inventors of the mechanical calculator.

Blaise Pascal.subject: Applied Sciences
Blaise Pascal.question: Following Torricelli and Galileo Galilei, in _____, he rebutted the likes of Aristotle and Descartes who insisted that nature abhors a vacuum
Blaise Pascal.fact: Following Torricelli and Galileo Galilei, in 1647, he rebutted the likes of Aristotle and Descartes who insisted that nature abhors a vacuum.

Boyle's law.subject: Applied Sciences
Boyle's law.question: The _____ was Relation between gas pressure and volume.
Boyle's law.fact: Boyle's law, also called the Boyle–Mariotte law or Mariotte's law (especially in France), is an empirical gas law that describes the relationship between pressure and volume of a confined gas. Boyle's law has been stated as: The absolute pressure exerted by a given mass of an ideal gas is inversely proportional to the volume it occupies if the temperature and amount of gas remain unchanged within a closed system.

Boyle's law.subject: Applied Sciences
Boyle's law.question: Boyle's law is named after Robert Boyle, who published the original law in _____
Boyle's law.fact: Boyle's law is named after Robert Boyle, who published the original law in 1662.

Buoyancy.subject: Applied Sciences
Buoyancy.question: The _____ was Upward force that opposes the weight of an object immersed in fluid.
Buoyancy.fact: Buoyancy (), or upthrust, is the force exerted by a fluid opposing the weight of a partially or fully immersed object (which may also be a parcel of fluid).

Buckling.subject: Applied Sciences
Buckling.question: The _____ was Sudden change in shape of a structural component under load.
Buckling.fact: In structural engineering, buckling is the sudden change in shape (deformation) of a structural component under load, such as the bowing of a column under compression or the wrinkling of a plate under shear. Euler's critical load and Johnson's parabolic formula are used to determine the buckling stress of a column.

Carlo Alberto Castigliano.subject: Applied Sciences
Carlo Alberto Castigliano.question: The _____ was Italian mathematician and physicist (1847–1884).
Carlo Alberto Castigliano.fact: Carlo Alberto Castigliano (9 November 1847, in Asti – 25 October 1884, in Milan) was an Italian mathematician and physicist known for Castigliano's method for determining displacements in a linear-elastic system based on the partial derivatives of strain energy.

Carlo Alberto Castigliano.subject: Applied Sciences
Carlo Alberto Castigliano.question: Alberto Castigliano moved from the region of his birth, Piedmont in northwestern Italy, to the Technical Institute of Terni (in Umbria) in _____
Carlo Alberto Castigliano.fact: Alberto Castigliano moved from the region of his birth, Piedmont in northwestern Italy, to the Technical Institute of Terni (in Umbria) in 1866.

Carlo Alberto Castigliano.subject: Applied Sciences
Carlo Alberto Castigliano.question: After three years of study in Turin, he wrote a dissertation in _____ entitled Intorno ai sistemi elastici ("About elastic systems") for which he is famous
Carlo Alberto Castigliano.fact: After three years of study in Turin, he wrote a dissertation in 1873 entitled Intorno ai sistemi elastici ("About elastic systems") for which he is famous.

A. W. F. Edwards.subject: Applied Sciences
A. W. F. Edwards.question: The _____ was British statistician and geneticist (born 1935).
A. W. F. Edwards.fact: Phylogenetic Inference, Selection Theory, and History of Science: Selected Papers of A. W. F. Edwards with Commentaries.

A. W. F. Edwards.subject: Applied Sciences
A. W. F. Edwards.question: Anthony William Fairbank Edwards, FRS (born 4 October _____) is a British statistician, geneticist and evolutionary biologist
A. W. F. Edwards.fact: Anthony William Fairbank Edwards, FRS (born 4 October 1935) is a British statistician, geneticist and evolutionary biologist.

A. W. F. Edwards.subject: Applied Sciences
A. W. F. Edwards.question: In _____ and 1964, Edwards, along with Luigi Luca Cavalli-Sforza, introduced novel methods for computing evolutionary trees from genetical data
A. W. F. Edwards.fact: In 1963 and 1964, Edwards, along with Luigi Luca Cavalli-Sforza, introduced novel methods for computing evolutionary trees from genetical data.

A. W. F. Edwards.subject: Applied Sciences
A. W. F. Edwards.question: To mark the Fisher centenary in _____, Edwards proposed a commemorative Sir Ronald Fisher window be installed in the Dining Hall of Gonville & Caius College
A. W. F. Edwards.fact: To mark the Fisher centenary in 1990, Edwards proposed a commemorative Sir Ronald Fisher window be installed in the Dining Hall of Gonville & Caius College.

A. W. F. Edwards.subject: Applied Sciences
A. W. F. Edwards.question: When the window was removed in _____, he vigorously opposed the move
A. W. F. Edwards.fact: When the window was removed in 2020, he vigorously opposed the move.

Abundance estimation.subject: Applied Sciences
Abundance estimation.question: The _____ was Group of statistical methods.
Abundance estimation.fact: Abundance estimation comprises all statistical methods for estimating the number of individuals in a population.

Accelerated failure time model.subject: Applied Sciences
Accelerated failure time model.question: The _____ was Parametric model in survival analysis.
Accelerated failure time model.fact: In the statistical area of survival analysis, an accelerated failure time model (AFT model) is a parametric model that provides an alternative to the commonly used proportional hazards models.

Adolphe Quetelet.subject: Applied Sciences
Adolphe Quetelet.question: The _____ was Belgian astronomer, mathematician, and sociologist (1796–1874).
Adolphe Quetelet.fact: Adolphe Quetelet also had a significant influence on Florence Nightingale who shared with him a religious view of statistics which saw understanding statistics as revealing the work of God in addition to statistics being a force of good administration.

Adolphe Quetelet.subject: Applied Sciences
Adolphe Quetelet.question: Adolphe studied at the Ghent Lycée, where he afterwards started teaching mathematics in _____ at the age of 19
Adolphe Quetelet.fact: Adolphe studied at the Ghent Lycée, where he afterwards started teaching mathematics in 1815 at the age of 19.

Analysis of covariance.subject: Applied Sciences
Analysis of covariance.question: The _____ was General linear model that blends ANOVA and regression.
Analysis of covariance.fact: Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) is a general linear model that blends ANOVA and regression.

Analysis of variance.subject: Applied Sciences
Analysis of variance.question: The _____ was Collection of statistical models.
Analysis of variance.fact: Analysis of variance (ANOVA) is a family of statistical methods used to compare the means of two or more groups by analyzing variance.

Ancillary statistic.subject: Applied Sciences
Ancillary statistic.question: The _____ was Statistic whose sampling distribution does not depend on the parameter.
Ancillary statistic.fact: An ancillary statistic has the same distribution regardless of the value of the parameters and thus provides no information about them. A ancillary statistic is a specific case of a pivotal quantity that is computed only from the data and not from the parameters.

Ancillary statistic.subject: Applied Sciences
Ancillary statistic.question: This concept was first introduced by Ronald Fisher in the 1920s, but its formal definition was only provided in _____ by Debabrata Basu
Ancillary statistic.fact: This concept was first introduced by Ronald Fisher in the 1920s, but its formal definition was only provided in 1964 by Debabrata Basu.

Anderson–Darling test.subject: Applied Sciences
Anderson–Darling test.question: The _____ was Statistical test.
Anderson–Darling test.fact: The Anderson–Darling test is a statistical test of whether a given sample of data is drawn from a given probability distribution.

Anderson–Darling test.subject: Applied Sciences
Anderson–Darling test.question: The test is named after Theodore Wilbur Anderson (_____–2016) and Donald A. Darling (1915–2014), who invented it in 1952
Anderson–Darling test.fact: The test is named after Theodore Wilbur Anderson (1918–2016) and Donald A. Darling (1915–2014), who invented it in 1952.

Arithmetic mean.subject: Applied Sciences
Arithmetic mean.question: The _____ was Type of average of a collection of numbers.
Arithmetic mean.fact: In mathematics and statistics, the arithmetic mean ( arr-ith-MET-ik), arithmetic average, or just the mean or average is the sum of a collection of numbers divided by the count of numbers in the collection. The term "arithmetic mean" is preferred in some contexts in mathematics and statistics because it helps to distinguish it from other types of means, such as geometric and harmonic.

Anscombe transform.subject: Applied Sciences
Anscombe transform.question: The _____ was Statistical concept.
Anscombe transform.fact: In statistics, the Anscombe transform, named after Francis Anscombe, is a variance-stabilizing transformation that transforms a random variable with a Poisson distribution into one with an approximately standard Gaussian distribution. The Anscombe transform is widely used in photon-limited imaging (astronomy, X-ray) where images naturally follow the Poisson law.

Archimedes.subject: Applied Sciences
Archimedes.question: The _____ was Greek mathematician and physicist (c. 287 – 212 BC).
Archimedes.fact: Archimedes of Syracuse ( AR-kih-MEE-deez; c. Archimedes anticipated modern calculus and analysis by applying the concept of the infinitesimals and the method of exhaustion to derive and rigorously prove many geometrical theorems, including the area of a circle, the surface area and volume of a sphere, the area of an ellipse, the area under a parabola, the volume of a segment of a paraboloid of revolution, the volume of a segment of a hyperboloid of revolution, and the area of a spiral.

Archytas.subject: Applied Sciences
Archytas.question: The _____ was 4th-century BC Greek philosopher, mathematician, astronomer and statesman.
Archytas.fact: Archytas (; Greek: Ἀρχύτας; 435/410–360/350 BC) was an Ancient Greek mathematician, music theorist, statesman, and strategist from the ancient city of Taras (Tarentum) in modern Apulia, Southern Italy. As a Pythagorean, Archytas believed that arithmetic (logistic), rather than geometry, provided the basis for satisfactory proofs, and developed the most famous argument for the infinity of the universe in antiquity.

Campdrafting.subject: Applied Sciences
Campdrafting.question: The _____ was Sport involving a horse and rider working cattle.
Campdrafting.fact: Campdrafting is a unique Australian sport involving a horse and rider working cattle. In a campdrafting competition, a rider on horseback must "cut out" one beast from the mob of cattle in the yard or the "camp" and block and turn the beast at least two or three times to prove to the judge that they have the beast under control; then take it out of the yard and through a course around pegs involving right and left hand turns in a figure eight, before guiding it through two pegs called "the gate".

Architectural drawing.subject: Applied Sciences
Architectural drawing.question: The _____ was Technical drawing of a building or building project.
Architectural drawing.fact: An architectural drawing or architect's drawing is a technical drawing of a building or building project that falls within the definition of architecture. Architectural drawings are used by architects and others for a number of purposes: to develop a design idea into a coherent proposal, to communicate ideas and concepts, to show clients the merits of a design, to assist a building contractor in construction based on design intent, to record the design and planned development, or to document ...

Conscription.subject: Applied Sciences
Conscription.question: The _____ was Compulsory enrollment into national or military service.
Conscription.fact: Conscription, also called the draft in American English and Philippine English, is the practice in which the compulsory enlistment in a national service, mainly a military service, is enforced by law. Conscription dates back to antiquity and it continues in some countries to the present day under various names.

Conscription.subject: Applied Sciences
Conscription.question: As of _____, many states no longer conscript their citizens, relying instead upon professional militaries with volunteers
Conscription.fact: As of 2025, many states no longer conscript their citizens, relying instead upon professional militaries with volunteers.

Drafting (aerodynamics).subject: Applied Sciences
Drafting (aerodynamics).question: The _____ was Aerodynamic technique.
Drafting (aerodynamics).fact: Drafting, or slipstreaming, is an aerodynamic technique where two moving objects are aligning in a close group to exploit the lead object's slipstream and thus reduce the overall effect of drag. Especially when high speeds are involved, as in motor racing and cycling, drafting can significantly reduce the paceline's average energy expenditure and can even slightly reduce the energy expenditure of the lead vehicle.

Draft (sports).subject: Applied Sciences
Draft (sports).question: The _____ was Process used to allocate certain players to sports teams.
Draft (sports).fact: A draft is a process used in some countries (especially in North America) and sports (especially in closed leagues) to allocate certain players to teams. In a draft, teams take turns selecting from a pool of eligible players.

Drafting (writing).subject: Applied Sciences
Drafting (writing).question: The _____ was Process to create preliminary versions of a written work.
Drafting (writing).fact: Drafting is the process by which preliminary forms of a written work are composed. Separate from other steps of the writing process, such as revision and editing, drafting involves the initial creation of the main content, structure, and style of a work.

Electrical drawing.subject: Applied Sciences
Electrical drawing.question: The _____ was Technical drawing in engineering.
Electrical drawing.fact: An electrical drawing is a type of technical drawing that shows information about power, lighting, and communication for an engineering or architectural project.

Engineering drawing.subject: Applied Sciences
Engineering drawing.question: The _____ was Type of technical drawing used to define requirements for engineered items.
Engineering drawing.fact: An engineering drawing is a type of technical drawing.

Plumbing drawing.subject: Applied Sciences
Plumbing drawing.question: The _____ was Type of technical drawing.
Plumbing drawing.fact: A plumbing drawing, a type of technical drawing, shows the system of piping for fresh water going into the building and waste going out, both solid and liquid. Mainly plumbing drawing consist of water supply system drawings, drainage system drawings, irrigation system drawings, storm water system drawings.

Hand spinning.subject: Applied Sciences
Hand spinning.question: The _____ was Method of turning fiber into thread.
Hand spinning.fact: The hand spinning movement that he initiated as a part of the Indian freedom struggle has made the handwoven cloth called "Khadi" made from handspun cotton yarn world-famous.

Hand spinning.subject: Applied Sciences
Hand spinning.question: In _____, it there was a discovery of plied cord spun by Neanderthals and dating back 41,000-52,000 years
Hand spinning.fact: In 2020, it there was a discovery of plied cord spun by Neanderthals and dating back 41,000-52,000 years.

Structural drawing.subject: Applied Sciences
Structural drawing.question: The _____ was Technical drawing detailing the specifications of a structure.
Structural drawing.fact: Structural drawings are commonly used across many branches of engineering and are illustrations depicting the specific design and layout of a building’s Structural elements. Structural drawings differ from architectural design as they mainly focus on how the building can be made as strong and stable as possible and what materials will be needed for this task.

Textile manufacturing.subject: Applied Sciences
Textile manufacturing.question: The _____ was Industry which produces textiles.
Textile manufacturing.fact: Textile manufacturing or textile engineering is a major industry.

Brain–computer interface.subject: Applied Sciences
Brain–computer interface.question: The _____ was Connection between brain and computer.
Brain–computer interface.fact: A brain–computer interface (BCI), sometimes called a brain–machine interface (BMI), is a direct communication link between the brain's electrical activity and an external device, most commonly a computer or robotic limb.

Brain–computer interface.subject: Applied Sciences
Brain–computer interface.question: Vidal's _____ paper introduced the expression brain–computer interface into scientific literature
Brain–computer interface.fact: Vidal's 1973 paper introduced the expression brain–computer interface into scientific literature.

Classical mechanics.subject: Applied Sciences
Classical mechanics.question: The _____ was Description of large objects' physics.
Classical mechanics.fact: In physics, classical mechanics is a theory that describes the effect of forces on the motion of macroscopic objects and bulk matter, without considering quantum effects, and often without incorporating relativistic effects either. The development of classical mechanics involved substantial change in the methods and philosophy of physics.

Classical physics.subject: Applied Sciences
Classical physics.question: The _____ was Category of theories.
Classical physics.fact: Classical physics consists of scientific theories in the field of physics that are non-quantum or both non-quantum and non-relativistic, depending on the context. In historical discussions, classical physics refers to pre-1900 physics, while modern physics refers to post-1900 physics, which incorporates elements of quantum mechanics and the theory of relativity.

Classical physics.subject: Applied Sciences
Classical physics.question: In historical discussions, classical physics refers to pre-_____ physics, while modern physics refers to post-1900 physics, which incorporates elements of quantum mechanics and the theory of relativit
Classical physics.fact: In historical discussions, classical physics refers to pre-1900 physics, while modern physics refers to post-1900 physics, which incorporates elements of quantum mechanics and the theory of relativity.

Computational physics.subject: Applied Sciences
Computational physics.question: The _____ was Numerical simulations of physical problems via computers.
Computational physics.fact: Computational physics is the study and implementation of numerical analysis to solve problems in physics. Historically, computational physics was the first application of modern computers in science, and is now a subset of computational science.

Continuum mechanics.subject: Applied Sciences
Continuum mechanics.question: The _____ was Branch of physics which studies the behavior of materials modeled as continuous media.
Continuum mechanics.fact: Continuum mechanics is a branch of mechanics that deals with the deformation of and transmission of forces through materials modeled as a continuous medium (also called a continuum) rather than as discrete particles. Continuum mechanics deals with deformable bodies, as opposed to rigid bodies.

Andron (architecture).subject: Applied Sciences
Andron (architecture).question: The _____ was Part of an ancient Greek house reserved for men.
Andron (architecture).fact: Andron (Greek: ἀνδρών, andrōn) or andronitis (ἀνδρωνῖτις, andrōnitis) is part of a Greek house that is reserved for men, as distinguished from the gynaeceum (γυναικεῖον, gynaikeion), the women's quarters. The andrōn was used for entertaining male guests.

Arcade (architecture).subject: Applied Sciences
Arcade (architecture).question: The _____ was Covered walk enclosed by a line of arches on one or both sides.
Arcade (architecture).fact: An arcade is a succession of contiguous arches, with each arch supported by a colonnade of columns or piers. Exterior arcades are designed to provide a sheltered walkway for pedestrians; they include many loggias, but here arches are not an essential element.

Arch.subject: Applied Sciences
Arch.question: The _____ was Curved structure that spans a space and may support a load.
Arch.fact: An arch is a curved vertical structure spanning an open space underneath it. Arches may support the load above them, or they may perform a purely decorative role.

Architectural style.subject: Applied Sciences
Architectural style.question: The _____ was Specific method of construction.
Architectural style.fact: An architectural style is a classification of buildings (and building structures) based on 84 characteristics and features, including overall appearance, arrangement of the components, method of construction, building materials used, form, size, structural style, and regional character. Architectural styles are frequently associated with a historical epoch (Renaissance style), geographical location (Italian Villa style), or an earlier architectural style (Neo-Gothic style), and are influenced...

Atrium (architecture).subject: Applied Sciences
Atrium (architecture).question: The _____ was Open-air or naturally-lit large space surrounded by a building.
Atrium (architecture).fact: In architecture, an atrium (pl.: atria or atriums) is a large open-air or skylight-covered space surrounded by a building. Atria were a common feature in Ancient Roman dwellings, providing light and ventilation to the interior.

Backyard.subject: Applied Sciences
Backyard.question: The _____ was Residential garden or other land behind a house.
Backyard.fact: A backyard, or back yard (known in the United Kingdom as a back garden or just garden), is a yard at the back of a house, common in suburban developments in the Western world.

Balconet.subject: Applied Sciences
Balconet.question: The _____ was False balcony.
Balconet.fact: Balconet or balconette is an architectural term to describe a false balcony, or railing at the outer plane of a window-opening reaching to the floor, and having, when the window is open, the appearance of a balcony. The wall-opening appearing alongside a balconette is called a French window.

Balcony.subject: Applied Sciences
Balcony.question: The _____ was Platform projecting from the wall of a building.
Balcony.fact: A balcony (from Italian: balcone, "scaffold") is a platform that typically projects from the wall of a building, supported by columns or console brackets, and enclosed with a balustrade, usually above the ground floor. Recessed balconies sit within the boundary of a buildings facade, so are the least exposed type of balcony.

Baldresca.subject: Applied Sciences
Baldresca.question: The _____ was Architectural element supporting loggia.
Baldresca.fact: A baldresca is an architectural element supporting a loggia. A baldresca has no columns.

Baluster.subject: Applied Sciences
Baluster.question: The _____ was Architectural element; vertical moulded shaft.
Baluster.fact: A baluster ( ) is an upright support, often a vertical moulded shaft, square, or lathe-turned form found in stairways, parapets, and other architectural features. A group of balusters supporting a guard railing, coping, or ornamental detail is called a balustrade.

Basement.subject: Applied Sciences
Basement.question: The _____ was Floor of a building which is below grade.
Basement.fact: A basement is any floor level of a building that is largely or completely beneath the ground. In cities with high property prices, such as London, basements are often fitted out to a high standard and used as living space.

Bathroom.subject: Applied Sciences
Bathroom.question: The _____ was Room for personal hygiene activities, such as showering.
Bathroom.fact: A bathroom is a room in which people wash their bodies or parts thereof.

Bedroom.subject: Applied Sciences
Bedroom.question: The _____ was Private room having at least one bed; used for rest or relaxation.
Bedroom.fact: A bedroom or bedchamber is a room situated within a residential or accommodation unit, primarily used for sleeping. A typical Western bedroom contains as bedroom furniture one or two beds, a clothes closet, and bedside table and dressing table, both of which usually contain drawers.

Bedroom.subject: Applied Sciences
Bedroom.question: The first coil spring mattress was not invented until _____
Bedroom.fact: The first coil spring mattress was not invented until 1871.

Bedsit.subject: Applied Sciences
Bedsit.question: The _____ was Accommodation of a room in a shared house.
Bedsit.fact: A bedsit, bedsitter, or bed-sitting room is a form of accommodation common in some parts of the United Kingdom which consists of a single room per occupant with all occupants typically sharing a bathroom. Bedsits are included in a legal category of dwellings called houses in multiple occupation (HMO).

Belt course.subject: Applied Sciences
Belt course.question: The _____ was Continuous row or layer of stones or brick set in a wall.
Belt course.fact: A belt course, also called a string course or sill course, is a continuous row or layer of stones or brick set in a wall. The belt course often projects from the side of the building.

Billiard room.subject: Applied Sciences
Billiard room.question: The _____ was Room with one or more billiard tables.
Billiard room.fact: A billiard room (also billiards room, or more specifically pool room, snooker room) is a recreation room, such as in a house or recreation center, with a billiards, pool or snooker table (The term "billiard room" or "pool room" may also be used for a business providing public billiards tables; see billiard hall.). The billiard room may be in the public center of the house or the private areas of the house.

Billiard room.subject: Applied Sciences
Billiard room.question: The earliest mention of pool as an indoor table game is in a _____ inventory list of the accounts of King Louis XI of France
Billiard room.fact: The earliest mention of pool as an indoor table game is in a 1470 inventory list of the accounts of King Louis XI of France.

Bonus room.subject: Applied Sciences
Bonus room.question: The _____ was Room in a house not meeting building codes.
Bonus room.fact: A bonus room, flex room, multiuse room or spare room (though the latter often means an extra bedroom) is a room created by remodeling or adding an addition that does not meet local building code definitions for traditional rooms, or is designed for multiple possible uses. Such a room might actually be intended for sleeping, but will be described as a "bonus room" in rental and sales listings.

Boudoir.subject: Applied Sciences
Boudoir.question: The _____ was Women's private sitting room.
Boudoir.fact: A boudoir ( boo-DWAR; French: [budwaʁ] ) is a lady’s private sitting room or salon in a furnished residence, usually between the dining room and the bedroom, but can also refer to a lady’s private bedroom. In later periods, the boudoir was used as a private drawing room, and was used for other activities, such as embroidery or spending time with one's husband.

Bressummer.subject: Applied Sciences
Bressummer.question: The _____ was Load-bearing beam in a timber-framed building.
Bressummer.fact: A bressummer, breastsummer, summer beam (somier, sommier, sommer, somer, cross-somer, summer, summier, summer-tree, or dorman, dormant tree) is a load-bearing beam in a timber-framed building. The use and definition of these terms vary but generally a bressummer is a jetty sill and a summer is an interior beam supporting ceiling joists, see below: (UK) In the outward part of the building, and the middle floors (not in the garrets or ground floors) into which the girders are framed.

Breezeway.subject: Applied Sciences
Breezeway.question: The _____ was Architectural feature.
Breezeway.fact: A breezeway is an architectural feature similar to a hallway that allows the passage of a breeze between structures to accommodate high winds, allow aeration, or provide aesthetic design variation. Often, a breezeway is a simple roof connecting two structures (such as a house and a garage); sometimes, it can be much more like a tunnel with windows on either side.

Breezeway.subject: Applied Sciences
Breezeway.question: One of the earliest breezeway designs to be architecturally designed and published was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright in _____ for the B. Harley Bradley House in Kankakee, Illinois
Breezeway.fact: One of the earliest breezeway designs to be architecturally designed and published was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright in 1900 for the B. Harley Bradley House in Kankakee, Illinois.

Buttery (room).subject: Applied Sciences
Buttery (room).question: The _____ was Originally a room under a monastery, in which food and drink were stored.
Buttery (room).fact: A buttery was originally a large cellar room under a monastery, in which food and drink were stored for the provisioning of strangers and passing guests. Nathan Bailey's An Universal Etymological English Dictionary gives "CELLARIST – one who keeps a Cella, or Buttery; the Butler in a religious House or Monastery." As the definition in John Stevens's The History of the Antient Abbeys shows, its initial function was to feed and water the guests rather than monks: "The Buttery; the Lodging for G...

Applied Thermal Engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Applied Thermal Engineering.question: The journal was established in _____ as Journal of Heat Recovery Systems and renamed to Heat Recovery Systems and CHP in 1987
Applied Thermal Engineering.fact: The journal was set up in 1981 as Journal of Heat Recovery Systems and renamed to Heat Recovery Systems and CHP in 1987.

Applied Thermal Engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Applied Thermal Engineering.question: According to the Journal Citation Reports, the journal has a _____ impact factor of 6.9
Applied Thermal Engineering.fact: According to the Journal Citation Reports, the journal has a 2021 impact factor of 6.9.

Automation engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Automation engineering.question: The _____ was Branch of engineering dealing with automated solutions to physical activities.
Automation engineering.fact: Automation engineering is a branch of engineering that deals with the development of methods and facilities that replace, in whole or in part, manual labour related to the control and monitoring of systems and processes.

Automotive engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Automotive engineering.question: The _____ was Discipline of engineering.
Automotive engineering.fact: Automotive engineering, along with aerospace engineering and naval architecture, is a branch of vehicle engineering, incorporating elements of mechanical, electrical, electronic, software, and safety engineering as applied to the design, manufacture and operation of motorcycles, automobiles, and trucks and their respective engineering subsystems. The automotive engineering field is research intensive and involves direct application of mathematical models and formulas.

Biochemical engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Biochemical engineering.question: The _____ was Manufacturing by chemical reactions of biological organisms.
Biochemical engineering.fact: Biochemical engineering, also called bioprocess engineering, is a field of study with roots stemming from chemical engineering and biological engineering.

Biochemical engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Biochemical engineering.question: It wasn't until _____, when Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin, that the field of biochemical engineering was established
Biochemical engineering.fact: It wasn't until 1928, when Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin, that the field of biochemical engineering was established.

Biomaterial.subject: Applied Sciences
Biomaterial.question: The _____ was Substance engineered for biological medical use.
Biomaterial.fact: A biomaterial is a substance that has been engineered to interact with biological systems for a medical purpose – either a therapeutic (treat, augment, repair, or replace a tissue function of the body) or a diagnostic one. The corresponding field of study is called biomaterials science or biomaterials engineering.

Bioresource engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Bioresource engineering.question: The _____ was Engineering subfield.
Bioresource engineering.fact: Bioresource engineering is an engineering discipline of researching, developing, and utilizing bioproducts. Bioresource engineering is more general and encompasses a wider range of technologies and various elements such as biomass, biological waste treatment, bioenergy, biotransformations, bioresource systems analysis, bioremediation and technologies associated with Thermochemical conversion technologies such as combustion, pyrolysis, gasification, catalysis, etc.

Broadcast engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Broadcast engineering.question: The _____ was Field of engineering dealing with radio and television broadcasting.
Broadcast engineering.fact: Broadcast engineering or radio engineering is the field of electrical engineering, and now to some extent computer engineering and information technology, which deals with radio and television broadcasting. Audio engineering and RF engineering are also essential parts of broadcast engineering, being their own subsets of electrical engineering.

Building services engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Building services engineering.question: The _____ was Professional engineering discipline.
Building services engineering.fact: Building services engineering (BSE), building services, service engineering or facilities and services planning engineering is a professional engineering discipline that strives to achieve a safe and comfortable indoor environment while minimizing the environmental impact of a building. Building services engineering can be considered a subdiscipline of utility engineering, supply engineering and architectural engineering (building engineering), which are all subsets of civil engineering.

Building services engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Building services engineering.question: The British Chartered Institution of Building Services Engineers (CIBSE) was founded in _____ and received a Royal Charter in the United Kingdom, formally recognising building services engineering as
Building services engineering.fact: The British Chartered Institution of Building Services Engineers (CIBSE) was set up in 1976 and received a Royal Charter in the United Kingdom, formally recognising building services engineering as a profession.

Car.subject: Applied Sciences
Car.question: The _____ was Motorised passenger road vehicle.
Car.fact: A car, or an automobile, is a motor vehicle with wheels. Most definitions of cars state that they run primarily on roads, seat 1-8 people, have four wheels, and mainly transport people rather than cargo.

Car.subject: Applied Sciences
Car.question: There are over 1.6 billion cars in use worldwide as of _____
Car.fact: There are over 1.6 billion cars in use worldwide as of 2025.

Car.subject: Applied Sciences
Car.question: The French inventor Nicolas-Joseph Cugnot built the first steam-powered road vehicle in _____, and the Swiss inventor François Isaac de Rivaz designed and constructed the first internal combustion-pow
Car.fact: The French inventor Nicolas-Joseph Cugnot built the first steam-powered road vehicle in 1769, and the Swiss inventor François Isaac de Rivaz designed and constructed the first internal combustion-powered automobile in 1808.

Car.subject: Applied Sciences
Car.question: The modern car—a practical, marketable automobile for everyday use—was invented in _____, when the German inventor Carl Benz patented his Benz Patent-Motorwagen
Car.fact: The modern car—a practical, marketable automobile for everyday use—was invented in 1886, when the German inventor Carl Benz patented his Benz Patent-Motorwagen.

Car.subject: Applied Sciences
Car.question: The _____ Oldsmobile Curved Dash and the 1908 Ford Model T, both American cars, are widely considered the first mass-produced and mass-affordable cars, respectively
Car.fact: The 1901 Oldsmobile Curved Dash and the 1908 Ford Model T, both American cars, are widely considered the first mass-produced and mass-affordable cars, respectively.

Ceramic engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Ceramic engineering.question: The _____ was Science and technology of creating objects from inorganic, non-metallic materials.
Ceramic engineering.fact: Ceramic engineering is the science of creating objects from inorganic, non-metallic materials.

Ceramic engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Ceramic engineering.question: Abraham Darby first used coke in _____ in Shropshire, England, to improve the yield of a smelting process
Ceramic engineering.fact: Abraham Darby first used coke in 1709 in Shropshire, England, to improve the yield of a smelting process.

Chemical reaction engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Chemical reaction engineering.question: The _____ was Subfield of chemical engineering.
Chemical reaction engineering.fact: Chemical reaction engineering (reaction engineering or reactor engineering) is a specialty in chemical engineering or industrial chemistry dealing with chemical reactors.

Chemical reaction engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Chemical reaction engineering.question: The term chemical reaction engineering was apparently coined by J.C. Vlugter while preparing the 1st European Symposium on Chemical Reaction Engineering which was held in Amsterdam in _____
Chemical reaction engineering.fact: The term chemical reaction engineering was apparently coined by J.C. Vlugter while preparing the 1st European Symposium on Chemical Reaction Engineering which was held in Amsterdam in 1957.

Clinical engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Clinical engineering.question: The _____ was Modern medical technologies.
Clinical engineering.fact: Clinical engineering is a specialty within biomedical engineering responsible for using medical technology to optimize healthcare delivery.

Clinical engineering.subject: Applied Sciences
Clinical engineering.question: The broader field of biomedical engineering also has a relatively recent history, with the first inter-society engineering meeting focused on engineering in medicine probably held in _____
Clinical engineering.fact: The broader field of biomedical engineering also has a relatively recent history, with the first inter-society engineering meeting focused on engineering in medicine probably held in 1948.
